newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senator proposes bonds for flood prevention.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senator proposes bonds for flood prevention.

text.p: A California state legislator has proposed a $400 million to $500 million bond measure that would pay for flood prevention programs in the state, his office said Thursday.

State Senator Jim Costa's proposed Flood Prevention Bond Act of 1998 would help fund flood control programs, build a system of bypasses and easements on the San Joaquin River, upgrade existing levees and other projects, his office said.
The legislation, Senate Bill 312, if approved by state lawmakers, would place the general obligation bond measure on the statewide ballot on Nov 3, 1998.
While the legislation does not specify a dollar amount, Costa said in a statement, "I anticipate starting in the range of $400-500 million, for discussion purposes."
The bond proposal, which will not be considered by the state legislature until mid-March, was introduced in the wake of January flooding in northern and central California.
Damages from the floods were estimated at over $1.5 billion, state officials said. The flooding damaged thousands of homes and businesses and inundated tens of thousands of acres of farmland.

Another measure introduced by Costa, who chairs the Senate Agriculture and Water Resources Committee, would appropriate state funds for costs not covered by the federal Natural Disaster Assistance Act to repair and rebuild flood-damaged roads, parks, utilities and other public facilities.
